card: This PR corrects HTTP status handling for malformed JSON-RPC 2.0 requests, returning HTTP 200 with an error object rather than HTTP 400. In debug builds with authenticated RPC, malformed JSON-RPC 2.0 requests trip an Assume assertion and crash bitcoind. In release builds, this fixes spec compliance by returning HTTP 200 and setting ID to null when parsing fails.
evidence: Author note in PR description: 'On master, the functional test in this PR actually crashes the node because the assumption is codified. Note that this crash requires: 1. RPC Authentication 2. A debug build'
Crash stack in PR description: "node0 stderr httprpc.cpp:46 UniValue JSONErrorReply(UniValue, const JSONRPCRequest &, HTTPStatusCode &): 'jreq.m_json_version != JSONRPCVersion::V2' check failed."
problem: Requests that properly specify JSON-RPC 2.0 but are otherwise malformed (e.g. missing method or invalid parameter types) fall into error-handling code that assumed version parsing failed. In debug builds, this violates an Assume check and crashes the node on authenticated requests; in release builds, it returns HTTP 400 instead of HTTP 200 required by JSON-RPC 2.0.

risk.why: Alters HTTP status codes and error serialization for malformed JSON-RPC requests, which could impact client error parsing.

summary: Fixes HTTP status code handling for malformed JSON-RPC 2.0 requests and ensures a null ID is provided when the request ID is missing. The RPC server now checks whether the request was identified as JSON-RPC 2.0 and returns HTTP 200 OK with an error payload instead of returning an HTTP 400 error status and triggering an assertion failure.
